title: Renting vs buying: it's a cash-flow question
concept: Buying can build equity, but it also ties up cash in a down payment, repairs, and illiquidity. Renting isn't 'throwing money away' — you're buying flexibility and predictable maintenance costs.
takeaway: Run the numbers for your city, timeline, and lifestyle.

scenario.situation: You might move cities in two years for work. You're tempted to buy 'to stop wasting rent.'

choices.text: Buy anyway — homes always appreciate fast
Rent for now; buying has high transaction costs for a short stay
Borrow the smallest down payment possible with an ARM

feedback.A: Homes can lag or dip. Short horizons amplify closing costs and risk.
feedback.B: Correct. Two years is often too short to overcome buying/selling friction.
feedback.C: Skinny down payments plus adjustable rates can amplify stress.

scenario.lesson: Match housing tenure to how long you'll actually stay.

title: What PITI actually means
concept: PITI is Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance — the core monthly housing payment many lenders quote. It still isn't the full cost: maintenance, HOA, utilities, and opportunity cost matter.
takeaway: Budget beyond the mortgage approval number.

scenario.situation: You're approved for a max mortgage that uses 43% of gross income for PITI.

choices.text: Spend the full approval — the bank did the math
Choose a lower payment so you can save and handle repairs
Skip insurance to lower the monthly

feedback.A: Banks estimate risk, not your life goals or surprise costs.
feedback.B: Correct. Breathing room beats being house-rich and cash-poor.
feedback.C: Insurance exists because rare events are catastrophic.

scenario.lesson: Approval limits are ceilings, not targets.

title: Equity is not spendable wealth (yet)
concept: Home equity is the gap between value and mortgage balance. It's real wealth, but it's trapped until you sell, refinance, or borrow against it — each with costs and risks.
takeaway: Don't treat HELOCs like a second checking account.

scenario.situation: Your home gained value and a lender offers a big HELOC for vacations and cars.

choices.text: Max it out — it's your money
Use HELOCs sparingly for value-add projects or true emergencies
Assume the home value will never dip

feedback.A: Borrowed equity has payments and risk if prices or income shift.
feedback.B: Correct. Cheap access to debt still is debt.

scenario.lesson: Equity is a balance sheet line, not a debit card.

title: REITs: real estate without landlord texts
concept: Real Estate Investment Trusts pool investor money to own properties or mortgages. You get liquidity and diversification without fixing a toilet at midnight.
takeaway: REITs can complement stocks; they're not a house substitute emotionally.

scenario.situation: You want real estate exposure but can't afford a down payment yet.

choices.text: Put everything into one local rental with zero reserves
Consider diversified REIT or real estate index funds while you save
Avoid real estate entirely until you buy a home

feedback.A: Illiquid assets plus zero reserves is how small problems become crises.
feedback.B: Correct. Public REITs are a simple on-ramp to the asset class.
feedback.C: You can learn the asset class before you buy a primary home.

scenario.lesson: Exposure can be liquid or illiquid — choose on purpose.

title: Closing costs: the bill nobody Instagrams
concept: Buyers often focus on down payment and forget title, escrow, recording fees, and prepaid items. Closing costs commonly run thousands beyond the down payment.
takeaway: Save an extra cushion beyond your target down payment.

scenario.situation: You saved exactly 10% down on a $400k home and nothing else.

choices.text: You'll figure out closing with a credit card if needed
Budget ~2–5% extra for closing costs and immediate move-in needs
Ask the seller to secretly lower the price after inspection

feedback.A: High-interest debt for closing costs erodes the wealth you're building.
feedback.B: Correct. Cash at close prevents desperate borrowing.
feedback.C: Negotiation is normal; 'secret' deals are a red flag and often impossible.

scenario.lesson: Under-save for closing and the deal can fall apart.
